requirement: In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
rationale: **Implementation.** The code appears to implement the requirement. - `protected_ranges` (src/lib.rs ~618–630) uses pulldown-cmark offset events. It protects `Start(CodeBlock)`, `Code`, `Html` and `InlineHtml` ranges. - `reference_roles` (~562) skips any `{` that `is_escaped` (odd count of preceding backslashes) or `is_protected`. - `definition_blocks` (~470) ignores colon-fence `{req}`, `{example}` and `{definition}` openers and closers that overlap code blocks. The legacy inline `{req}` role is never recognised as a definition, because only colon fences are parsed. **Tests that exist.** - `code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal` (src/lib.rs ~729) covers four things: inline code containing `{req}`, a `:::{req}` inside a fenced code block, a legacy `{req}` role, and a real directive that still renders. - `markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal` (~808) covers three cases for `{impl}` references: inline code, a fenced block and a backslash-escaped role. It asserts that all three stay literal and that no badge is produced. - `tests/definitions.rs` (~205 and ~326) covers the same three cases for `{term}` references. It also checks that a literal reference does not become a validation input. **Gap.** The requirement explicitly lists raw HTML as a case where role-looking text must stay literal. The implementation handles it through `Event::Html` and `Event::InlineHtml`, but I found no test with role-looking text inside raw HTML, either block-level or inline. My searches of src/lib.rs and tests/ for HTML-related fixtures found nothing. That leaves one of the requirement's named cases unverified. No FIXME or other source comment acknowledges the gap, so I can't choose FIXME. Adding a test with a reference inside `…` or an HTML block would close it.
